# requireNonNaN

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not the `NaN` number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonNaN() — Returns the value after checking that it is not the `NaN` number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonNaN<T>(
  value: T | number,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is not NaN."
): T;
```

Nothing is coerced first, which is where this differs from the global `isNaN`: that one converts its argument, so `isNaN("abc")` and `isNaN(undefined)` both report `true`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                      | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                        | `T \| number` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is not NaN."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with the `NaN` number excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                      |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is the `NaN` number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonNaN(0); // => 0
requireNonNaN("abc"); // => "abc"
requireNonNaN(NaN); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonNaN(0 / 0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
